texts: good. "occur" adds no separate event - both moon-phase times sit directly on the spring tide - and the "or" is kept intact rather than resolved to one phase. One caveat that needs no rewrite: a disjunction is stored opaquely, so a bare "when does a spring tide occur?" will not bind either phase on its own, though a question about the pair will.

bad: "The Keepers" - a capitalized plural - is read by the translator's rules as a proper name, so the parse both invents a group of keepers it is barred from asserting and omits the name it would need, leaving the Keepers inconsistent with the "a Keeper" of your other sentences. Lowercase it and they parse as the body of keepers you mean: "The keepers time the salt-bloom harvest to the new-moon spring tide." One further note: "time X to Y" is stored with the bare preposition "to", which the reasoner's purpose bridge can read as an aim you never stated, so "schedule X for Y" is the safer verb.
